newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Japan rubber mixed, firm yen may cap prices.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Japan rubber mixed, firm yen may cap prices.

text.p: Japan's rubber futures market is likely to be mixed and will probably drift within limited ranges as the yen's firmer trend against the dollar could put a lid on prices, traders said on Monday.

"Technical factors indicate the markets have more room to rise, but private investors will be wary of making fresh purchases due to the yen's rebound on the dollar and a lack of bullish factors," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
Despite a slight drop in Japan's rubber stocks at the end of October, lingering uncertainty as to whether domestic stocks have hit a ceiling could also weigh on the markets, they said.
The benchmark April contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended Monday's morning session at 142.4 yen per kilogramme after closing at 143.2 yen on Friday.
Meanwhile, the benchmark April contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was 142.5 yen per kg in the second morning session, down from 143.3 yen on Friday.
Another trader noted that TOCOM's benchmark April contract could hover around 142 or 143 yen this week.
One focus point for the market will be the amount of rubber submitted for certification for delivery against the November contract, which expires later this month.

The deadline for submission to TOCOM is later today. One source said if a large quantity of rubber is submitted, it could indicate ample supplies in the physical market, which would potentially be a bearish factor.
Otherwise, activity this week could be spurred by technical factors.

Reflecting recent sluggish market conditions, open interest in TOCOM rubber futures fell to 214,183 lots as of last Friday, down from 230,401 lots as of October 2 and 398,742 lots at the end of January this year.

A lack of fresh incentives and easing demand/supply conditions in Japan, combined with investors' shift to commodities which are more volatile, were the main reasons behind the decrease in open interest, traders said.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted at around $1.25 on a free-on-board (FOB) basis as of Monday, flat against that of November 5.

In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 154 yen per kg on Monday, little changed from November 5. -- Keiko Takagi, Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
